Shown in [fig-ex-basis] are two vectors $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_2$ in the plane $\real^2$.

Vectors $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_2$ in $\real^2$.

Explain why $\bcal=\{\vvec_1,\vvec_2\}$ is a basis for $\real^2$.

Using [fig-ex-basis], indicate the vectors $\xvec$ such that

$\coords{\xvec}{\bcal} = \twovec{2}{-1}$

$\coords{\xvec}{\bcal} = \twovec{-1}{-2}$

$\coords{\xvec}{\bcal} = \twovec{0}{3}$

Using [fig-ex-basis], find the representation $\coords{\xvec}{\bcal}$ if

$\xvec = \twovec{-2}{-1}$.

$\xvec = \twovec{2}{4}$.

$\xvec = \twovec{2}{-5}$.

Find $\coords{\xvec}{\bcal}$ if $\xvec=\twovec{60}{90}$.
